subject: AI & Agents
title: Hallucinations: When AI Makes Things Up
description: A short lesson to help you apply Hallucinations: When AI Makes Things Up.

hook.text: Ask an LLM for a source and it invents a real-sounding paper that doesn't exist.

buildup.text: Hallucinations happen when the model generates plausible-sounding but factually wrong content.

discovery.text: The model predicts likely next tokens. If the truth is unlikely, it generates something plausible instead.

twist.text: Hallucinations are confident. The AI doesn't signal uncertainty — it states fiction as fact.

climax.text: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) helps by grounding responses in real documents.

punchline.text: It doesn't know what it doesn't know.

quiz.question: Why do LLMs hallucinate?
options: They predict plausible tokens even when truth is unlikely
Their memory gets corrupted over time

details.summary: Hallucinations occur when an LLM generates confident, fluent text that is factually wrong or entirely fabricated. The model has no mechanism for distinguishing truth from plausible fiction in its outputs.
details.whyItMatters: Hallucinations undermine trust in AI and can cause real harm: fake legal citations, incorrect medical advice, and fabricated sources. Understanding why they happen is essential for safe AI use.
takeaways: LLMs generate plausible text regardless of factual accuracy
They have no internal mechanism to verify truth
Hallucinations are a fundamental limitation, not a fixable bug

faq.question: Why do LLMs hallucinate?
faq.answer: LLMs are trained to generate statistically likely text, not verified truth. When the model lacks knowledge, it fills gaps with plausible-sounding content rather than admitting ignorance. The architecture has no fact-checking step.

faq.question: Can hallucinations be prevented?
faq.answer: Reduced but not eliminated. RAG grounds responses in source documents. Reasoning models check their own work. But all current LLMs hallucinate sometimes, making human verification essential for high-stakes uses.
